 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the appellants/owners challenging the judgment and award dated 01.03.2011 in MVC.No.6047/2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, for seeking setting aside the aforesaid judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts :
On 10.01.2009, at about 4.30 p.m., the deceased Narayana was traveling in the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-02-T-1137 & KA-02-T-1138 along with one Mr.
Galihanumantharayappa.

The driver of the said vehicle was driving the same in high-speed and in a rash and negligent manner from Kumbalgod-Kanakapura Road,
when they reached near Agara Hosapalya Cross, the driver of the said tractor and trailer drove the same in high speed on a road hump, due to which the deceased fell down and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased and he died on the spot.
Therefore, the claimants being the parents and younger brother of the deceased have filed the claim petition seeking compensation.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the records.
4.

In the present case, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation and fixed the liability on the owners (respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein) who are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

5. Ex.P1 is the FIR with complaint, in which, it is alleged that the driver of tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-02-T-1137 & KA-02-T-1138 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the deceased fell down and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased and the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
6. The father of the deceased has given the evidence.
Though he may not be the eye witness, but narrated the accident and how the deceased died in the said accident.

Ex.P2 is the Spot Mahazar,
which shows the involvement of the tractor and trailer in the accident.

Ex.P4 is the Panchanama which proves that while the deceased was traveling in the tractor and trailer, fell down and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased and the deceased died.

sentences.text: Ex.P5 is the post mortem report which shows that the deceased died due to the injuries sustained to the stomach in the accident.
Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which is the result of investigation that the deceased died in the accident as described above.
8. RW2 is the eye witness to the accident.

He had stated that the driver of the tractor and trailer drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and due to which, the deceased fell on the road and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased.
Therefore, all these evidence on record conclusively prove that the deceased died in the accident as stated above.
The appellant No.2 is examined as RW1.
RW2 stated that the deceased was traveling in the tractor and trailer, but denied the factum of accident due to rash and negligence.

RW1 in his evidence has stated that the deceased was waiting near Agara Hosapalya bus stand and since, he was known to RW1, he allowed the deceased to travel in the tractor and while traveling in the tractor, the deceased fell down and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased.

Therefore, from the evidence of RW1,
it is proved that the deceased was traveling in the tractor and trailer and the deceased died in the accident.
Therefore, while re-appreciating the evidence on record, as discussed above, it is conclusively hold that the deceased died in the said accident.

Appellant No.2 though he was driving the tractor and trailer himself stated that the deceased has travelled in the tractor and trailer and the deceased fell down on the road and the back wheel of the tractor and trailer ran over the deceased and the deceased succumbed to the injuries, which is proved from the evidence of RW1 who is appellant No.2 herein.
Therefore, it is proved that the deceased died in the road traffic accident that occurred on 10.01.2009 at about 4.30 p.m., near Agara Hosaplaya Cross.
Therefore, I do not see any perversity or illegality in the findings framed by the Tribunal in this regard.

REGARDING QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
9.
Even though, the Tribunal determined the compensation is on lesser side, but there is no appeal by the claimants.
Upon considering the compensation determined by the Tribunal, it is found to be just and proper and there are no grounds available to enhance the quantum of compensation.
The claimants have not preferred the appeal.
Therefore, the claimants are satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, even insofar as quantum of compensation awarded, there are no grounds available for interference with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, over all, there are no grounds available to cause interference with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is dismissed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 01.03.2011 in MVC.No.6047/2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, is hereby confirmed.
iii. No order as to costs.
